title: The History of Batman Arkham | From Asylum To Arkham Shadow | Gaming History
description: The full history of the Batman Arkham games: Rocksteady's Asylum, City and Knight, the Origins prequel, the passing of Kevin Conroy, Suicide Squad and Arkham Shadow in 2024.

sections.heading: The Dark Knight finally gets a great game
sections.script: For decades, superhero games were mostly rushed tie ins, and Batman was no exception. Then a studio called Rocksteady made a game that changed everything. Batman: Arkham Asylum arrived in twenty oh nine and showed what a Batman game could be, with smart fighting, stealth, detective work and a twisted madhouse to explore. Over the next six years, the Arkham series grew from a single island prison into an entire open city, and from there into a Gotham full of tanks and fear gas. In this video we trace the full history of Batman Arkham: the three Rocksteady games, the prequel from another studio, the sad loss of the man who voiced Batman, and the games that came after. Put on the cowl, because the night is long.

sections.heading: Arkham Asylum
sections.script: Arkham Asylum was developed by Rocksteady and written by Paul Dini, a veteran Batman writer. The whole game takes place on Arkham Island, where the Joker lets himself be captured, then takes over the asylum and traps Batman there. The voice cast came from the beloved animated series: Kevin Conroy as Batman, Mark Hamill as the Joker and Arleen Sorkin as Harley Quinn. The game mixed three skills in a new way. Free flow combat made fights feel like a dance, predator rooms let you hunt enemies from the shadows, and Detective Mode showed clues and hidden things. Warner Bros said in September twenty oh nine that more than two and a half million copies had been shipped to stores, and Guinness World Records named it the most critically acclaimed superhero game ever, with an average review score of ninety one point six seven.

sections.heading: Arkham City opens the doors
sections.script: Rocksteady's next step was bold. Arkham City, released in October twenty eleven, turned a section of Gotham itself into a giant prison district, run by Hugo Strange. Batman could now glide and grapple across an open city, finding side missions about villains like the Riddler, Penguin and Mr. Freeze. The story, set eighteen months after Asylum, had a terrible twist, because the Joker was dying of the Titan formula and infected Batman with the same illness. Warner Bros said that around four point six million copies shipped in the first week, with about two million sold directly to customers, and by February twenty twelve it had shipped six million. Downloadable content also let you play as Catwoman, Nightwing and Robin. Many fans still call Arkham City the best superhero game ever made.

sections.heading: Arkham Origins takes a turn
sections.script: Rocksteady was busy planning its next move, so a different studio, WB Games Montreal, developed Arkham Origins in twenty thirteen. It was a prequel set eight years before Asylum on one snowy Christmas Eve, when a crime boss named Black Mask puts a price on Batman's head and eight assassins arrive in Gotham. It showed a younger, rougher Batman, and the story included his first meeting with the Joker. Since Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill did not return, Roger Craig Smith and Troy Baker took their places. It was also the first game in the series to have multiplayer, which was made by Splash Damage. Opinions on Origins are mixed, because many felt it played it safe, but its story has some fans, and its post credits scene teased a Suicide Squad.

sections.heading: Arkham Knight and the Batmobile
sections.script: Rocksteady returned to close the story with Arkham Knight, released on June twenty third, twenty fifteen for PlayStation 4, Xbox One and computers. For the first time, Batman could drive the Batmobile through a much larger Gotham, which was evacuated because Scarecrow threatened the city with fear gas. The mysterious Arkham Knight hunted Batman, and the Joker lived on as a hallucination in his head. The game looked stunning and had a big, emotional ending, with extra content on Batgirl, Red Hood and others. Unfortunately, the computer version launched in a terrible technical state, and Warner Bros pulled it from sale a day later. It took months to return, and the studio apologised. The console versions, however, were praised, and the game closed the trilogy with a bang.

sections.heading: Remasters, VR and side stories
sections.script: Beyond the main games, the Arkham world grew in many directions. Arkham City Lockdown and a mobile version of Origins were fighting games from the creators of Mortal Kombat. Origins Blackgate was a side scrolling adventure for handheld systems. In twenty sixteen, Batman: Return to Arkham brought remastered versions of Asylum and City to PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, using the Unreal Engine four. That same year, Rocksteady launched Batman: Arkham VR, a short virtual reality story that let you actually feel like the Dark Knight in the cave. The series had become a large, connected universe fans called the Arkhamverse, with books, comics and an animated film. All of it was built around one thing: the hunt for the Joker and the fate of Batman.

sections.heading: Losing the voice of Batman
sections.script: In November twenty twenty two, the gaming and animation world was heartbroken when Kevin Conroy, the voice of Batman for so many years, passed away at the age of sixty six. He had voiced Batman in the animated series, in the Arkham trilogy and in many other projects. His co star Mark Hamill described him as the definitive Batman for generations. For the Arkham fans, his voice was inseparable from the character. The games gave him some of his most memorable lines, and the performance in Arkham Knight is often described as one of his best. His final turn as Batman in the Arkhamverse came in a game that arrived after his passing, which we will talk about next.

sections.heading: Suicide Squad and Gotham Knights
sections.script: After Arkham Knight, Rocksteady worked for years on a new game. It was revealed in twenty twenty as Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League, and it was set after Arkham Knight, in the same universe. It follows Harley Quinn, Deadshot, Captain Boomerang and King Shark, and it supports four player co op. The release was delayed more than once, and it finally launched on February second, twenty twenty four. Reaction was disappointing, with players criticising the live service design. In the meantime, WB Games Montreal released Gotham Knights in twenty twenty two, a game about the Bat Family after Batman dies, but set in a different continuity than the Arkham games. Both games showed that many fans still wanted the style and tone of the earlier trilogy.

sections.heading: Arkham Shadow
sections.script: The Arkham story got a surprise return in twenty twenty four. On October twenty first, Arkham Shadow was released exclusively on the Meta Quest three virtual reality headset. It was made by Camouflaj, the studio behind the Iron Man VR game, and published by Oculus Studios. The story is a direct sequel to Arkham Origins, set six months later, with Roger Craig Smith back as Batman. It follows Batman as he faces a new villain called the Rat King on the Fourth of July. Players punch, throw batarangs and sneak around in first person. Many reviewers called it the best virtual reality game on the headset. It was also a reminder that the Arkham formula works just as well when you feel like you are inside the cowl.

sections.heading: The legacy of the Arkhamverse
sections.script: Today, the Arkham series is still the standard by which superhero games are measured. It proved that a licensed character could carry a serious, polished game, and its combat system was copied by many other action adventures. It balanced fear, power and detective work so well that fans still talk about the first time they were hunted by the Scarecrow or the first time they glided over Gotham. We have no official news on a brand new Rocksteady Batman game, so we will not guess. For now, the trilogy remains available, and the memory of Conroy and Hamill lives on. Now it is your turn. Which Arkham game is your favourite, and who is your favourite villain? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for more franchise histories.
